subject: Air-gapped KMS failover & minimal-egress playbook — review and redlines
messages:
From: Olivia Perez <olivia.perez@fjordbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fjordbank.com
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: air-gapped KMS failover and egress-minimization playbook

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. FjordBank is moving ahead with a PoC for a fully air-gapped private deployment of Redwood for our high-risk payments processing environment. Our security team asked for a concrete playbook that covers:

- Key provisioning and BYOK handoff for an HSM-backed KMS (operator separation requirements)
- Offline failover procedures (air-gap cutover, removable-media key backup, ceremony steps)
- Minimal egress constraints and allowed telemetry/attestation flows for a no-internet environment
- Rotation cadence, emergency rekey, and evidence collection for audits (SOC2 & internal)
- Roles and access (who holds which key material, escrow options)

Can you share a draft playbook and call out any non-starters from Redwood's side? We attached our high-level requirements (fjord-reqs-20271005.pdf). Ideally we want something we can rehearse in a dry-run within 3 weeks.

Olivia Perez
Director, Infrastructure Security
FjordBank

Attachment: fjord-reqs-20271005.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Perez <olivia.perez@fjordbank.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: air-gapped KMS failover and egress-minimization playbook

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear requirements and the PDF. I pulled together a focused draft that addresses each of your bullets; attached: redwood-playbook-draft.md. High-level summary:

- BYOK handoff: support for customer-provided encrypted key blobs that are unsealed in an HSM-bound key ceremony. We require a split-operator model (minimum 2 operators) and offline paper/USB backup escrow stored in customer custody.
- Offline failover: phased steps to transition to an isolated HSM-only serving mode, with explicit steps for removable-media export, integrity checks, and a documented offline unseal ceremony.
- Egress minimization: default posture is zero outbound except for signed attestation pings to a preconfigured DMZ collector over a highly restricted proxy. We describe a deterministic minimal telemetry schema (hashes + status codes) to preserve auditability while keeping data off-network.
- Rotation & emergency rekey: normal rotation is planned as an offline ceremony every 90 days; emergency rekey flow (triggered by compromise indicators) includes immediate key-generation on a new HSM, re-encryption of persistent caches, and a rollback plan.
- Evidence & audit: guidance on collecting signed event logs from the HSM and local attestation bundles for SOC2 reviewers.

Open questions for FjordBank:
1) Will operator personnel perform the offline ceremony on-site, or should Redwood's operator be present under an escrowed observation model?
2) Are you able to host a secure jump-host for operator access during rehearsals (bastion-only, no general egress)?

I'm proposing a short workshop to walk through the ceremony steps; available Wed/Thu next week.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-playbook-draft.md (text/markdown)
From: Olivia Perez <olivia.perez@fjordbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fjordbank.com
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: air-gapped KMS failover and egress-minimization playbook

Jordan — this is great, thanks. Quick clarifications before the workshop:

- We expect Fjord operator personnel to run the ceremony; Redwood staff can observe and validate. Is that supported in the draft?
- For attestation pings: we need the exact minimal schema (no PII, only hashes/timestamps, and a signed fingerprint). Can you produce that as an appendix?
- Audit evidence: SOC2 requires log export in a verifiable format. Does the HSM you recommend support signed event log bundles we can store offsite?

Proposed workshop: Thu 10/14 10:00 AM ET.

Olivia
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, mina_haddad@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: air-gapped KMS failover and egress-minimization playbook

Looping in a couple of small technical clarifications that should go into the next draft: 

- Key rotation cadence: recommend separating access-key rotation (every 90 days) from master-key ceremonies (every 12 months) unless an emergency rekey is invoked. Call out the operators required for threshold unseal and keep the master-key material offline.
- HSM recommendations: include model options with FIPS+CC EAL ratings and note firmware attestation support (we should include attestation-patterns-diagram.png).
- Cache invalidation: when rotating, ensure local KV caches are tombstoned and re-seeded under the new key to avoid serving mixed-key artifacts.

I'll update the draft with a short appendix for the minimal telemetry schema and the event-log export format.

Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: attestation-patterns-diagram.png (image/png)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: air-gapped KMS failover and egress-minimization playbook

A couple of operational notes to fold in before sending to FjordBank: 

- Minimal egress path: recommend a push-only signed hash collector in the DMZ that accepts only TLS with client certs; no general HTTP/S egress from the air-gapped cluster. The collector stores only (timestamp, node-id, HSM-fingerprint, SHA256-status-hash).
- Failover modes: primary == HSM-backed serving with ephemeral caches; fallback == HSM-only serving (no cache writeback) to preserve confidentiality if network blockers activate. Document explicit steps to switch modes and run sanity checks.
- Emergency procedure: require an out-of-band verification (phone/video + 3 operator approvals) before importing backup key material from removable media.

Also: procurement note — some of the higher-assurance HSMs have longer lead times. If FjordBank needs an accelerated window, we should identify acceptable model flexibility now.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Perez <olivia.perez@fjordbank.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, security@fjordbank.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Consolidated playbook draft & next steps — air-gapped KMS failover

Olivia — thanks for the questions and team input. I attached the consolidated version: redwood-airgap-playbook-v1.pdf. Key changes since the initial draft: 

- Appendix A: minimal telemetry schema (signed, hash-only) suitable for SOC2 evidence without data leakage.
- Appendix B: offline ceremony checklist with explicit operator roles, required artifacts, and acceptance criteria.
- Appendix C: HSM model recommendations and firmware attestation pattern (diagram included).
- Clear separation of rotate vs. master-ceremony cadences; emergency rekey flow with out-of-band approvals.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm operator model (Fjord operators run ceremony; Redwood observes) — reply here with an "operator_ok" or "rdw_observe_ok" preference.
2) Workshop Thu 2027-10-14 10:00 AM ET to walk the ceremony and rehearse the failover checklist.
3) Rehearsal window target: 3 weeks after workshop.

If that aligns, we'll lock the workshop invite and circulate the runbook rehearsal plan.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-airgap-playbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
